evidence.title: Navigate stable and freshly authorized Command Work Queue pages
evidence.goal: Replace inaccessible after-first-50 Command records with a bounded, revocation-safe, same-route read-only cursor while preserving existing six views, host ACL and current filter/sort/selection.
outputs: Read-only opt-in second/subsequent pages, limited to currently authorized 50 visible rows, with safe next cursor and first page return on same route.
Generic fail-closed revocation and stale-context error without new authorization or pagination datastore.
acceptance_tests: 123 authorized rows + denied and cross-tenant rows paginate as 50/50/23 with unique stable ordering and no unpermitted source references.
Every page fresh host session and all current source per-object ACLs; revoked owner changes invalidate cursor without partial data.
Selection only current page; invalid/duplicated/malformed cursor denied before session/owner; stale cursor 404, no privilege from token.
Browser same-route next/first navigation preserves filter/sort and contextually escapes source values; existing pre-page JSON shape for <=50 preserved.
Exact SHA Ubuntu/macOS/Windows work queue tests and mandatory engineering-kernel checks including unchanged security-critical 90% floor.

rules: Canonical owner: Command CAP-CMD-101 Unified Work Queue §§3, 8–11, 14–17, 21, 25. Command owns Incident/Task rows and the exact six system views; Shared owns final Saved Views; final Inspector is separate. The canonical Pagination Filtering Sorting contract names cursor/stable order/limits but does not yet fix a public cursor wire schema.

Engineering owner: existing epic E10-CMD-101 → task E10-CMD-101G-PAGE; dependency E10-CMD-101F-SELECTION IMPLEMENTED, not accepted. Git parent only PR #164 frozen HEAD 75981f08712978cf5f0555cad7639f37b3439486; PR #164 belongs to separate CAP-CMD-109 freshness epic and remains unmerged and L2-reviewed independently. The parent SHA is immutable.
Code owner: product-runtime/work-queue (Go), reusing existing exact six-view Project and one authenticated GET /command/work-queue, first-party SessionResolver and per Incident/Task Owner.CanRead.
Former behavior: 5000 candidates scanned and individually authorized, sorted, then only first 50 accessible. No HTTP or HTML mechanism to retrieve the remaining authorized rows.
